subject: health
title: My Feelings
about: Naming feelings (happy, sad, angry, scared, tired, proud), seeing that people can feel differently about the same thing, and using calm words, I-messages and slow breaths. This is the first unit of NC Grade 1 mental and emotional health (1.MEH.1) and the start of the school year.
tip: Ask him to make the face for each feeling before he taps the answer.

cards.q: A friend shares a toy with you. How do you feel?
cards.note: Sharing can make both of you feel happy.

cards.q: Your ice cream falls on the ground. How might you feel?
cards.note: It is okay to feel sad. Feelings come and go.

cards.q: Someone grabs your crayon without asking. How might you feel?
cards.note: It is okay to feel angry. Use words to say so.

cards.q: A big dog barks very loudly. How might you feel?
cards.note: It is okay to feel scared. Tell a grown-up.

cards.q: It is late and you keep yawning. How do you feel?
cards.note: Tired is a feeling too. Sleep helps your body.

cards.q: You learn to tie your shoes all by yourself. How do you feel?
cards.note: Proud means you feel good about what you did.

cards.q: You see a friend with tears and a frown. How do they feel?
cards.note: Tears and a frown often mean sad. You can ask, are you okay?

cards.q: You are angry. What is a good way to show it?
cards.note: Try saying, I feel angry, and then say why.

cards.q: You want a turn on the swing. What do you say?
cards.note: Asking nicely helps you get a turn.

cards.q: Someone says, I feel sad when you leave me out. What kind of message is this?
cards.note: An I-message says how you feel and why.

cards.q: What kind of voice helps you share your feelings?
cards.note: A calm voice helps people listen to you.

cards.q: Can two kids feel differently about the same thing?
cards.note: One kid may love thunder. Another may not. Both are okay.

cards.q: You feel very angry. What can help your body calm down?
cards.note: Breathe in slowly. Breathe out slowly. Try it three times.

cards.q: You feel sad or worried. What can you do?
cards.note: Grown-ups can help with big feelings.
